elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry or termination
elements.evidence: within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination, return all Customer Data

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems
and certify such deletion in writing
for up to six (6) months (exceeds and therefore encompasses 90 days)
within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination, return all Customer Data

reasons: The inserted 10.3 supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and deletion plus written certification thereafter.

The 'at Customer's request' condition attaches only to limb (a) transition assistance; the mandatory 30-day data return in limb (b) and the deletion/certification in limb (c) are unconditional, so the request condition does not swallow the data-return obligation.

The return deadline runs from expiry or termination rather than from a later request or notice, matching the preferred trigger, and the duties trigger on termination of the Agreement rather than of an individual Order Form.

Minimality is satisfied: the rule expects a clause that was entirely absent from Section 10, and the fix is a single concise inserted paragraph that leaves 10.1 and 10.2 (access wind-down, Deliverable delivery, refunds) untouched with no undefined terms or dangling mechanics.
Note only in rationale, not as a deviation: 'reasonable' modifies transition assistance, a mild qualifier that does not defeat any preferred element.
